Describe.your.nutrient.budget.calculatio:
Due to the bidirectional flow at Wetland Stream Outflow, nutrient load reduction will be calculated in a few ways dependent on surface water elevation of Buckeye Lake (Figure #) and flow of Murphy’s Run. 

When the AV sensor deployed at Murphy’s Run is giving positive flow values, meaning Murphy’s Run is the main inflow, AND Buckeye Lake surface elevation is < 891 ft, inflow is BROP_01 and outflow is BROP_03. When the AV sensor is giving positive flow values AND Buckeye Lake surface elevation is > 891 ft, inflow is BROP_01 and outflow is BROP_06. In both of these situations, load reduction occurring in the West Pool is already accounted for because water leaving the West Pool makes it back into wetland stream and is accounted for in nutrient concentration of BROP_03 and BROP_6. 

When the AV sensor deployed at Murphy’s Run is giving negative flow values, meaning Buckeye Lake is the main inflow, AND Buckeye Lake surface elevation is < 892 ft, inflow is BROP_07 and outflow is BROP_06. Like when the AV sensor is reading positive flow values, load reduction occurring in the West Pool is already accounted for because water leaving the West Pool makes it back into wetland stream and is accounted for in nutrient concentration of BROP_6. 

A rare situation could occur in which Buckeye Lake backs up so far it can backfill into the West Pool. Therefore, when the AV sensor deployed at Murphy’s Run is giving negative flow values AND Buckeye Lake surface elevation > 892 ft, inflow is BROP_07 and outflow is BROP_02. In addition, since water making it over to the West Pool is unlikely to flow back into the lake as a result of lake level generating back pressure, a load reduction can be calculated based on inflow as BROP_07 and outflow as BROP_05 using a flow rate of the pump to generate volume times concentration. This load reduction calculation using BROP_05 is added to load reduction from BROP_07 vs BROP_02 in this scenario.

Describe.your.nutrient.budget.calculatio:
Since Burntwood Langenkamp has relatively clear inputs and output structures (Figure 2), nutrient load reduction will be calculated as [inflow concentration X inflow volume] - [outflow concentration X outflow volume]. Inflow and outflow concentrations will be obtained from surface water samples. Inflow and outflow volumes will be calculated using the water level control structure areas, the HOBO water level data, and information about the pump rate. 

Nearby USGS river gauge stations will be used to estimate how much of Burntwood Creek flows are intercepted and captured by the wetland. The nearby USGS Station – Chickasaw Ck (drainage area = 16.4 mi2) flow data is utilized to calculate Burntwood Creek streamflows for the Burntwood Creek drainage area 8.91 mi2) at the wetland inflow using a multiplication factor of 0.54.  USGS Station - Coldwater Ck (drainage area = 11.4 mi2) station is also an option for this estimation as an alternative to the Chickasaw Ck station, and the watershed weight multiplication factor compared to Burntwood Creek is 0.78 or 1.28. Percentage of Burntwood Creek flows captured by the wetland will be calculated as a function of inflow rate wetland divided by Burntwood Creek streamflow.

Describe.your.nutrient.budget.calculatio:
The two pools will be treated as independent Wetlands in order to calculate load reductions for both the Great Miami River and Spring Creek. With the method, a few assumptions are made including water does NOT flow from North Pool to South Pool, when it does during periods of high flow. Another assumption being made is that no groundwater flow is occurring, when in fact it is likely a large amount of groundwater flow is occurring due to sandy soils. 

For Spring Creek, nutrient load reductions will be calculated [inflow volume x inflow concentration] - [outflow volume x outflow concentration]. Inflow volumes are calculated by watershed weighting the Troy Great Miami River USGS Station with a multiplication factor of 0.028. Outflow volume is calculated from the daily difference in pool volume using Solinst water levelogger data and a bathymetry survey. Inflow and outflow concentration is obtained from monthly sampling trips and assumed to stay constant until the next sampling event. 

For the Great Miami River, nutrient load reductions will be calculated [inflow volume x inflow concentration] - [outflow volume x outflow concentration]. Inflow volumes are calculated by watershed weighting the Troy Great Miami River USGS Station with a multiplication factor of 0.996. Outflow volume is calculated from the daily difference in pool volume using Solinst water levelogger data and a bathymetry survey. Inflow and outflow concentration is obtained from monthly sampling trips and assumed to stay constant until the next sampling event.

Describe.your.nutrient.budget.calculatio:
A HOBO level logger deployed in the Tipp City wetland records water depth every 30 minutes from which an average daily water depth is calculated. Daily pool volume is calculated using data from a recent bathymetry survey completed by Donnie Knight of US Fish & Wildlife where volume of water according to acre foot corresponds to variation in depth (Figure X.3). Acreage corresponds to the total number of acres at a given corresponding depth at the time of survey. Note that volume is the total gallons of water calculated using 326,000 gallons of water per acre foot. Daily pool volume is calculated using the equation: volume = 326,000 x depth (ft) x acres  where depth acres is the acreage corresponding to the water depth. Change in daily pool volume is calculated by subtracting the previous day’s pool volume from the current pool volume. All of the positive changes in pool volume (inflows) were added together over a season to obtain total seasonal inflows.

Two sampling locations within the wetland (Wetland Inflow and Mid Wetland) were averaged to obtain an average ”Wetland” nutrient concentration. Seasonal average nutrient concentrations were calculated for the Great Miami River Upstream and “Wetland”. Differences between the Great Miami River Upstream and Wetland were calculated and multiplied by total inflows over the season to determine seasonal nutrient load reduced.
